problem_type: Balance snapshots lose the resource identity of the endpoint
symptom: Onboarding cannot show account funds and the send balance reader returns the key limit.
direct_cause: Both readers queried the key endpoint exclusively.
class_root: The read boundary did not distinguish account funds from a per-key allowance.
affected_population: APIMart onboarding and account balance readers
entry_points: Credential save, foreground refresh and send-side account snapshot

external_sources.purpose: Identify the owner of the token-balance response
Identify the owner of the user-balance response

invariants: Only an explicit account zero can trigger a top-up.
Onboarding never computes credits from a positive amount with an unspecified unit.

door_reduction.why_not: The two resources require separate named results. Seed declaration, lookup, IPC, credential mutation, preload, and presentation each retain their role.

generality_proof: Both onboarding paths receive named snapshots from the same guarded reader. The account-only IPC reads the same account resource.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Resolve the credential once, enforce the official origin and authorize both GET paths.
Decode each response by subject. Preserve explicit credits independently of unlabelled amounts; only a key can be unlimited.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Ordinary IPC returns account funds only.
The candidate check rejects only explicit key authentication refusals.

recurrence.reason: Account and key limits can diverge on every read.
same_class_scan: door-map on both public readers identifies save, recheck and snapshot paths
rg remainCredits traces the check rows, top-up branch and Composer receipt

prevention.invariant: Each named snapshot comes only from its declared resource.
prevention.strategy: Resolve one guarded reader and bind responses by requested path.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove the mapping from token allowance to the account-only IPC.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The local response contract owns resource identity. Existing fetch and authorization dependencies are sufficient.

migration: Snapshots are transient and stored credentials and projects need no migration.
residual_risks: Loopback tests exercise official response shapes without a live funded account.
